claim: The writer census recomputed from what the census read out of the objects, rather than inferred from the two equipment attributes the index carries.
value: Real World Value Mapping Storage: unresolved implementation 1.3.6.1.4.1.22213.1.143 / 0.5 20; Key Object Selection Document Storage: dcm4che 40; Grayscale Softcopy Presentation State Storage: unresolved implementation 1.3.6.1.4.1.22213.1.143 / 0.5 624, dcm4che 462; Parametric Map Storage: highdicom 691; Comprehensive SR Storage: unresolved implementation 1.3.6.1.4.1.22213.1.143 / 0.5 1,656, dcm4che 462; Comprehensive 3D SR Storage: highdicom 5,408; RT Structure Set Storage: unresolved implementation 1.3.6.1.4.1.22213.1.143 / 0.5 17,901, dcm4che 1,432, DCMTK 25
status_note: Attribution is by ImplementationClassUID (0002,0012) first, then ImplementationVersionName (0002,0013), then a ContributingEquipmentSequence item, with the deciding attribute recorded per row. The highdicom and PixelMed signatures were read out of those toolkits' own source; the DCMTK and dcm4che signatures are asserted from observed values and are labelled so.
notes: The file meta names the library that serialised the dataset. It is not a claim about what produced the analysis, and for an archive that re-encodes on ingest it names the last writer rather than the first.

claim: Where both carriers name a toolkit, they disagree about who wrote the object more often than they agree.
value: 1,292 of 1,388 scored objects disagree: Comprehensive SR Storage declares PixelMed, file meta says unresolved implementation 1.3.6.1.4.1.22213.1.143 / 0.5, 1,292 objects
status_note: An object is scored only when the toolkit named by the equipment attributes has a file-meta signature established independently of this corpus. Toolkits with no registered expectation are never scored either way.
notes: Observation, not a resolution. Re-encoding on ingest and a different serialisation backend would both produce this and nothing measured here distinguishes them.
